reminder.notes:
Reliability fixes from the v2.19.61 two-device logs

### Features
- The diagnostics log now records the exact time each alarm was armed for, a one-line roster of every armed reminder and its next fire time after each reconcile, and a line each time the background worker starts. A missed reminder can now be traced to whether this device was holding an alarm for that moment at all.
- Duplicate copies of a LAN message are dropped on arrival. Each action was sent three times for reliability and applied three times on the receiving phone.

### Bug fixes
- Location reminders are no longer reported as having a missing alarm on every check. The check could only see clock alarms, so a perfectly healthy geofence was re-armed endlessly and the health counter permanently showed a failure that was not there.
- Instant Wi-Fi sync of reminder edits between phones now works. It was sending the entire database in one message on every change, which was far too large to fit, so nothing was ever delivered over Wi-Fi and every edit waited for the cloud.
- Snoozing or completing a reminder no longer loses track of the alarm it just set. The app could hold an alarm it did not know about, so a reminder deleted or completed on the other phone could still ring here.

ai-scanner.notes:
AI Scanner 1.4.1 — Background update checks, and no more double-downloading updates

### Features
- AI Scanner now checks for updates periodically in the background (about every 6 hours) and posts a notification when one is found, in addition to the existing manual "Check for Updates" in Settings. Tapping the notification opens the app; the download and install still happen from the Settings sheet.

### Bug fixes
- The update downloader now persists its in-flight DownloadManager id and re-attaches to a still-running download instead of deleting the partial file and starting over — fixes re-downloading the same update from zero after backgrounding or reopening the app mid-update.
- The update sheet now re-syncs its progress on resume instead of occasionally showing a frozen progress bar.

mirrordrive.notes:
Show the app version and PNSJY branding in Settings

Settings now ends with the current app version and the PNSJY store branding, so every
PNSJY app presents the same footer.

### Features

- The Settings screen now shows the installed app version and a PNSJY brand footer as its
  last two items, consistent across all PNSJY apps.

### Bug fixes

No user-facing bug fixes in this release.

bchat.notes:
BChat 0.3.0-beta.4 - private delivery beyond one device

This beta completes BChat's public-relay privacy architecture. Message and file
content remains end-to-end encrypted, delivered content is retained only on
user devices, and the relay removes bounded pending ciphertext after recipient
acknowledgement.

### Features

- Public TLS relay with bounded offline ciphertext and encrypted resumable file
  storage that is deleted after authenticated device delivery.
- Data-only FCM wake-up so a closed Android app can collect and decrypt pending
  messages without exposing message content to Google.
- Accountless QR device linking, signed device revocation, remote local-data
  wipe, and encrypted contact/group state transfer without copying history.
- Secure group messaging with membership key rotation and bounded prior epochs.
- Device-local encrypted attachments, configurable retention, storage usage,
  readable key-free JSON export, and privacy lifecycle cleanup.
- Encrypted profile photos and a complete profile screen.
- Native SMS and messaging-app invite sharing with tap-to-open Android links.

### Bug fixes

- Invalid first-device authorisations no longer create relay account state.
- The certificate-chain root device can no longer be accidentally unlinked.
- Oversized linked-device snapshots are split into bounded relay-safe chunks.
- Remote unlink now clears messages, files, keys, trust pins and profile data in
  both foreground and closed-app execution.
- Onboarding no longer asks for obsolete Bluetooth permissions.
